title: NFR-003 fail-closed: an unavailable idempotency store blocks the mutation rather than risking a duplicate
risk: With the dedup store down the platform cannot tell a retry from a new action, so it either double-sends or refuses all legitimate traffic.
preconditions: Namespace gov-nfr-<case_id>-<worker_id>; NFR verification runs against the offline gateway with mock SoR and channel boundaries.
Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; failure, outage and crash injections are scripted at the substituted boundary, never faked inside the assertion.
The idempotency store is scripted to be unavailable during the middle phase.

steps.expected: Exactly one effect and one receipt.

steps.action: Take the store down and dispatch a new action
steps.expected: The dispatch is blocked with a typed fail-closed error; the adapter counter does not advance, so no unkeyed action escapes.

steps.action: Restore the store and replay the original request
steps.expected: The durable dedup record blocks a second effect and returns the original receipt.
One effect, one receipt, no orphan delivery.

assertions: An unavailable dedup store blocks mutating external actions instead of degrading to no protection.
The block is scoped to mutating actions: read-only skills still serve during the outage.
After restoration the replay is deduped by the durable record, not re-executed.
Exactly one external effect exists at the end of the timeline.
forbidden: Failing open so retries can proceed while dedup is down.
Blocking reads as well and turning a dedup outage into a total outage.
Discarding the pending action silently so the customer never receives anything and nobody knows.
evidence: Fail-closed error record and the read-path success during the outage.
cleanup: Delete gov- rows and restore the store script.
automation: Core PEP, rules engine, audit writer, idempotency store and worker lease logic run as real code under test; only ERP/WMS, channel gateways, Redis and the model provider are substituted. Faults are injected at those boundaries and waits are condition-based on persisted state.
